Order 
In compliance of earlier order dated 24.03.2022, counsel for respondents has filed IA No.1153/2022, which is an application for correction in the name of respondent No.3 as Dilip Singh instead of Ram Kishore which has wrongly been mentioned.
2. For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.
3. At this stage, learned Claims Tribunal is directed to incorporate the name of Dilip Singh in place of Ram Kishore- respondent No.3 which has wrongly been typed.

4. This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company u/S 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 20.12.2012 passed by Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Ambah District Morena [in short "Claims Tribunal"] in MACC No.105/2011 seeking exoneration from its liability to pay compensation to respondents/claimants.

sentences.text: As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the death of Kailash Rathore, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,37,000/- along-with interest in favour of Claimants from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

7. Learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company filed this appeal on the ground that award passed by Claims Tribunal is against the settled principle of law and also against the material available on record.

Learned Claims Tribunal has completely erred in accepting the dependency of respondent Nos. 2 & 3 on the deceased and it is further submitted Claims Tribunal has also erred in rejecting the defence of appellant/Insurance Company regarding violation of the policy of insurance company.

Appellant witness specifically stated before the Claims Tribunal that insured vehicle being driven without permit, fitness and licence at the time of occurrence of alleged accident, but Claims Tribunal has not accepted the same.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of award passed by learned Claims Tribunal and it is further prayed that Insurance Company be exonerated from its liability.

8. On the other hand, counsel for respondents/claimants supported the impugned award and submitted that Claims Tribunal has passed the award after due appreciation of evidence, therefore,
no interference is required and prayed for dismissal of appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

9. Heard counsel for parties and perused the record.
10.

On perusal of the record, it was found that claimants/respondents filed seizure memo (Ex.P-8)
and according to the seizure memo, police seized the fitness certificate bearing No.0808630 which was valid up to 03.03.2012.
Police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17041 3 MA-345-2013 has also seized the driving licence (MP 07/20040007562) which was in the name of Dinesh Sharma, who is driver of the alleged vehicle.

But, appellant/Insurance Company has failed to examine from concerned RTO about the driving licence of the driver was valid and effective or not and also failed to prove the fitness certificate validity which was valid up to 03.03.2012.
11.

It is settled principle of law that it is the duty of Insurance Company to prove that owner and driver of alleged vehicle had breached the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and it must be proved as per law.

When fitness certificate and driving licence were seized by the police, which was produced by claimants with appeal, so it is the duty of Insurance Company to prove that these documents were not valid and effective by way of evidence to call from concerned RTO.

But,
Insurance Company has failed to do so.

12. In considered opinion of this Court, appellant/Insurance Company has failed to prove by way of evidence that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective licence and at the time of alleged accident, there is no fitness of the alleged vehicle.
13. With aforesaid discussion, appeal filed by Insurance Company has no substance and being bereft of merit, is hereby dismissed.
14. A copy of this order be sent to Claims Tribunal for information and necessary compliance.
